title: betaLB: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
text: Generates profile likelihood confidence intervals standardized regression coefficients (beta) effect sizes, including multiple correlation, semipartial correlations, improvement R-squared, squared partial correlations, differences standardized regression coefficients, Cohen’s f-squared, models fitted lm(). intervals invert Gaussian likelihood-ratio test covariance matrix outcome regressors, normal-theory robust (fourth-moment) cutoff.

title: betaLB: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
text: example, multiple regression model fitted using program quality ratings (QUALITY) regressand/outcome variable number published articles attributed program faculty members (NARTIC), percent faculty members holding research grants (PCTGRT), percentage program graduates received support (PCTSUPP) regressor/predictor variables using data set 1982 ratings 46 doctoral programs psychology USA (National Research Council, 1982). Likelihood-based confidence intervals standardized regression coefficients generated using BetaLB() function betaLB package.

what: Fit the regression model using the lm() function.
title: betaLB: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
code: object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)

what: Estimate the standardized regression slopes and the corresponding likelihood-based confidence intervals.
title: betaLB: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
code: BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05) #> Call: #> BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05) #>  #> Standardized regression slopes with MVN likelihood intervals: #>            est   2.5%  97.5% #> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3423 0.6394 #> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2395 0.5426 #> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.1179 0.4148

title: betaLB: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
text: package provides following functions. coef(), confint(), summary(), print() methods available returned objects. effect-size functions take output BetaLB() use type control. Scalar targets use profile-likelihood regions; multi-coefficient targets use conservative vector projection, output names calibration dimension. unverified endpoint NA; Wald endpoint substituted. Robust calibration assumes independently sampled random regressors finite fourth moments. Examples function package vignettes.

title: betaLB: Example Using the BetaLB Function
text: type = "mvn", cutoff assumes multivariate normality. type = "robust", cutoff scaled sample fourth moments intervals require normality. solver runs per significance level alpha.
code: std_mvn <- BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01)) std_robust <- BetaLB(object = object, type = "robust", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01)) std_robust #> Call: #> BetaLB(object = object, type = "robust", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01)) #>  #> Standardized regression slopes with ROBUST likelihood intervals: #>            est   0.5%   2.5%  97.5%  99.5% #> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3173 0.3611 0.6228 0.6611 #> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2083 0.2530 0.5294 0.5726 #> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.0670 0.1154 0.4175 0.4684

title: betaLB: Example Using the BetaLB Function
text: print(), summary(), coef(), confint() methods available. confint() method accepts levels (1 - alpha) computed. covariance matrix defined likelihood-based intervals, vcov() stops message.
code: summary(object = std_robust, alpha = 0.05) #> Call: #> BetaLB(object = object, type = "robust", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01)) #>  #> Standardized regression slopes with ROBUST likelihood intervals: #>            est   2.5%  97.5% #> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3611 0.6228 #> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2530 0.5294 #> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.1154 0.4175 coef(object = std_robust) #>    NARTIC    PCTGRT   PCTSUPP  #> 0.4951451 0.3914887 0.2632477 confint(object = std_robust, level = 0.95) #>             2.5 %    97.5 % #> NARTIC  0.3610731 0.6227540 #> PCTGRT  0.2530089 0.5294304 #> PCTSUPP 0.1153935 0.4174637

title: Estimate Standardized Regression Coefficients and the Corresponding Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals — BetaLB
text: Partition covariance matrix outcome regressors $$\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \begin{pmatrix} \sigma^{2}_{y} & \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{yx}^{\prime} \\ \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{yx} & \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x} \end{pmatrix}.$$ standardized regression slopes $$\beta^{\ast}_{j} = \beta_{j} \frac{\sigma_{x_{j}}}{\sigma_{y}}, \quad \boldsymbol{\beta} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x}^{-1} \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{yx}.$$ Let \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{S}}\) sample covariance matrix divisor \(n\), \(q\) number variables, $$F \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right) = n \left[ \log \left| \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right| - \log \left| \tilde{\boldsymbol{S}} \right| + \operatorname{tr} \left( \tilde{\boldsymbol{S}} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1} \right) - q \right]$$ Gaussian likelihood-ratio statistic \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{S}}\). target \(\theta = g \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right)\), \(\beta^{\ast}_{j}\), \(100 \left( 1 - \alpha \right) \%\) interval $$\left\{ \theta_{0} : \min_{\boldsymbol{\Sigma} : g \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right) = \theta_{0}} F \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right) \leq c \, \chi^{2}_{1, 1 - \alpha} \right\}.$$ type = "mvn", \(c = 1\). type = "robust", $$c = \frac{\boldsymbol{b}^{\prime} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{ADF}} \boldsymbol{b}}{\boldsymbol{b}^{\prime} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{N}} \boldsymbol{b}}, \quad \boldsymbol{b} = \frac{\partial g}{\partial \operatorname{vech} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right)},$$ evaluated \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{S}}\), \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{N}}\) \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{ADF}}\) normal-theory fourth-moment estimates asymptotic covariance matrix \(\sqrt{n} \operatorname{vech} \left( \tilde{\boldsymbol{S}} \right)\). vector target dimension \(r\), \(c\) largest generalized eigenvalue \(\boldsymbol{B} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{ADF}} \boldsymbol{B}^{\prime}\) relative \(\boldsymbol{B} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{N}} \boldsymbol{B}^{\prime}\) cutoff \(r\) degrees freedom. effect size functions use statistic \(g\). intervals sets parameter values likelihood-ratio test covariance matrix response regressors reject significance level alpha. type = "mvn", divisor-\(n\) Gaussian covariance likelihood chi-square cutoff used. type = "robust", cutoff scaled sample fourth moments data, intervals robust non-normality. asymptotic procedures, without finite-sample coverage guarantee. solver runs per significance level. effect size functions (RSqLB(), SCorLB(), PCorLB(), DeltaRSqLB(), FSqLB(), DiffBetaLB()) take object returned function use type control.
